# Typhus

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Infectious diseases > Zoonoses and vector-borne diseases > Typhus*

[Original Article Link](/library/NH0-qh)

---

## Summary

Typhus is an umbrella term for three zoonitic diseases caused by bacteria in the family Rickettsiaceae. <u>Endemic</u> (murine) typhus is caused by <u>Rickettsia typhi</u> transmitted by rat and cat <u>fleas</u>. <u>Epidemic typhus</u> is caused by <u>Rickettsia prowazekii</u> transmitted by the body <u>louse</u>. <u>Scrub typhus</u> is caused by <u>Orientia tsutsugamushi</u> transmitted by <u>chiggers</u>. All three types of typhus manifest with <u>flu-like symptoms</u> and can cause a <u>maculopapular rash</u> that spreads from the trunk to the extremities. Symptoms in <u>epidemic typhus</u> are often more severe and can include neurological symptoms (e.g., <u>seizures</u>). Features unique to <u>scrub typhus</u> include <u>lymphadenopathy</u> and <u>eschar</u> that can develop at the site(s) of infection. <u>Confirmatory testing</u>, e.g., with an <u>indirect fluorescent antibody</u> (<u>IFA</u>) test, is not required before starting treatment for clinically suspected cases. <u>Doxycycline</u> is the first-line treatment for all types of typhus, and early treatment can mitigate the severity of illness and complications.

---

## Endemic (murine) typhus

<u>Epidemic typhus</u> and <u>scrub typhus</u> are described separately.




### Background [[2]](/library/_VY5CL)




* <u>Epidemiology</u>: occurs worldwide; mainly in warm coastal regions, e.g., southern US and Hawaii

* <u>Pathogen</u>: <u>Rickettsia typhi</u>

* Transmission: : exposure to infected rat and cat <u>fleas</u>  [[3]](/library/VxWGvn0)

* <u>Incubation period</u>: 7–14 days [[2]](/library/_VY5CL)





### Clinical features [[2]](/library/_VY5CL)




* <u>Fever</u>, severe <u>headache</u>, <u>malaise</u>

* <u>Maculopapular</u> or <u>petechial</u> <u>rash</u> erupts on the trunk and spreads to the extremities (palms and soles are spared).  [[2]](/library/_VY5CL)

* <u>Nausea</u>, <u>vomiting</u>, abdominal <u>pain</u>

* <u>Cough</u>

* <u>Altered mental status</u>





> [!NOTE]
> The <u>rash</u> of Typhus starts on the Trunk.




### Diagnostics [[3]](/library/VxWGvn0)




Suspect the diagnosis in patients with clinical features and relevant exposure history.




* Routine studies

* <u>CBC</u>: <u>leukocytosis</u> or <u>leukopenia</u>, <u>anemia</u>, <u>thrombocytopenia</u>

* <u>Liver chemistry</u>: ↑ <u>ALT</u> and <u>AST</u> (3–5 times <u>ULN</u>), ↓ <u>albumin</u> [[3]](/library/VxWGvn0)

* <u>Inflammatory markers</u>: ↑ <u>ESR</u>

* <u>Confirmatory tests</u>

* <u>Gold standard</u>: <u>IFA test</u> demonstrating a four-fold rise in rickettsial <u>antibodies</u> when comparing a sample taken during the first week of illness to a convalescent sample taken 2–4 weeks later.

* Other modalities, e.g.: <u>enzyme immunoassay</u> (<u>EIA</u>), <u>PCR</u>, and <u>Weil-Felix test</u>





> [!TIP]
> Consider reporting suspected cases to the state or local health department (based on local practice).




### Treatment [[2]](/library/_VY5CL)




Initiate treatment early in all clinically suspected cases.




* First-line: <u>doxycycline</u> DOSAGE  [[2]](/library/_VY5CL)

* Alternatives (e.g., during <u>pregnancy</u>): <u>chloramphenicol</u> or a <u>quinolone</u> [[3]](/library/VxWGvn0)

---

## Epidemic typhus

<u>Murine typhus</u> and <u>scrub typhus</u> are described separately.




### Background [[2]](/library/_VY5CL)




* <u>Epidemiology</u>

* Most common in central and eastern Africa, central and South America, and Asia  [[2]](/library/_VY5CL)[[4]](/library/gxWFDn0)

* Extremely rare in the US

* <u>Pathogen</u>: <u>Rickettsia prowazekii</u>

* Transmission: direct contact with persons and/or fabrics infested with human <u>body lice</u>  [[2]](/library/_VY5CL)

* <u>Incubation period</u>: 8–16 days [[2]](/library/_VY5CL)

* Recrudescent infection (Brill-Zinsser disease) [[4]](/library/gxWFDn0)

* Reactivation of <u>latent infection</u> with <u>R. prowazekii</u> that occurs months to years after the initial infection

* Triggered by extreme <u>stress</u> or <u>immunosuppression</u>; unrelated to <u>louse</u> <u>infestation</u>





![Rickettsia prowazekii](media/ij57s0nwbx34tuw9a7e80usk.jpg)

Rickettsia prowazekii




### Clinical features [[4]](/library/gxWFDn0)




Acute infections and <u>Brill-Zinsser disease</u> have similar clinical presentations.




* Abrupt onset of <u>fever</u>, severe <u>headache</u>, <u>malaise</u>, <u>myalgia</u>, abdominal <u>pain</u>, <u>nausea</u>, <u>cough</u>

* <u>Maculopapular</u> or <u>petechial</u> <u>rash</u> that spreads from the trunk to the extremities 4–5 days after the onset of <u>fever</u> [[2]](/library/_VY5CL)

* Neurological symptoms (e.g., confusion, <u>coma</u>, <u>seizures</u>) and/or <u>vasculitis</u> in advanced untreated disease





> [!NOTE]
> The <u>rash</u> of Typhus starts on the Trunk.




### Diagnostics [[2]](/library/_VY5CL)




Suspect the diagnosis in patients with clinical features and relevant exposure history, or a history of prior infection.




* Routine studies [[4]](/library/gxWFDn0)

* <u>CBC</u>: <u>thrombocytopenia</u>

* <u>BMP</u>: ↑ <u>BUN</u>

* <u>Liver chemistry</u>: ↑ <u>ALT</u> and <u>AST</u>, ↑ <u>bilirubin</u>

* <u>Confirmatory tests</u>: for acute and recrudescent infections 

* <u>IFA test</u> demonstrating a four-fold rise in rickettsial <u>antibodies</u> when comparing a sample taken during the first week of illness to a convalescent sample taken 2–4 weeks later.

* Other modalities, e.g.: <u>EIA</u>, <u>PCR</u>, <u>Weil-Felix test</u>  [[4]](/library/gxWFDn0)





### Treatment




Initiate treatment early in all clinically suspected cases.




* First-line: <u>doxycycline</u> DOSAGE  [[2]](/library/_VY5CL)

* Alternative (e.g., during <u>pregnancy</u>): <u>chloramphenicol</u> [[4]](/library/gxWFDn0)
